title: The description is the trigger
caption: The AI sees only the name and description up front, and the description decides when the skill loads.

scent.title: Did you know?
scent.text: Information scent: the cue on a label that tells you whether it leads where you want to go.
scent.source: Pirolli and Card, Xerox PARC, 1999: a finding about people searching. Borrowing it for the AI is an inference.

footer.quote: “If the description doesn't convey when the skill is useful, the agent won't know to reach for it.”
footer.coding: At startup the agent reads only name and description from each SKILL.md; the body stays closed.

alt.scene: The control room from the pilot's chair. Left, the captain says: We've reached a new site. The pilot sits at the console; through the window, a marker buoy at the new site. Beside him the manual's index is open: four skills, each a name and a one-line description, two of them vague. Behind the index, five procedure cards stand fanned out, shut and greyed.

description-carries-the-whole-burden.description: because only name and description load at startup, "the description carries the entire burden of triggering. If the description doesn't convey when the skill is useful, the agent won't know to reach for it" [1].

descriptions-and-information-scent.description: Pirolli and Card's abstract names "information scent models, which address the identification of information value from proximal cues" [1]. It is a finding about people foraging for information; that a vague label gives a model less to go on is an inference, not their finding. The page-646 definition was read second-hand.

the-pilots-view.title: The pilot's view
the-pilots-view.script: Sit in the model's chair for a second. At the start of a task it has every skill's name and description in front of it, and none of the instructions behind them, like a pilot with the index open and every card closed. So unless you call the skill by name, the description is the trigger: it decides whether the model picks the skill on its own.

two-entries.title: Two entries
two-entries.script: Take two descriptions for the same skill: "Samples", and "Take a sediment sample at a new site". A task comes in, because we have just reached a new site. Which one would you open?

scent.title: Scent
scent.script: Researchers who study how people search call this information scent: the cue on a label that tells you whether it leads where you want to go. They found it in people, and I am lending it to the model. So your job is to make the description smell like the task it serves, because that scent is what pulls the trigger.
